the EEG coherence elicited by visual noise and auditory noise, modulated by quasi Brownian noise, exhibits a maximum for a particular level of the auditory or visual noise.

the present investigation documents that the electrophysiology of the human brain is characterized by a multisensory internal SR phenomenon, in which the EEG's GWC is enhanced by an intermediate level of sensory noise in the auditory or the visual modality.
the present study provides the first experimental evidence of the occurrence of MISR in human EEG, which is a promising tool to investigate the neural mechanisms of multisensory integration.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multisensory internal SR is an important mechanism that may contribute to the optimal integration of sensory information in human cognition.
multisensory internal SR is an emergent property that can be elicited in the human EEG.
the occurrence of MISR of EEG's GWC can be considered as a novel electrophysiological phenomenon of multisensory processing in humans.

a specific level of auditory or visual noise can be considered as optimal to improve EEG coherence in the presence of the other sensory modality.
the human EEG coherence, as computed by GWC, is enhanced by a particular level of input noise.
